## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** `LimitResetModel.js` behaves as the description states. Empty fetches keep queued deadlines, a nonempty response replaces that provider's future deadlines, due entries survive a refresh that races the 15-second timer, disabled providers are dropped at announce time, and provider IDs that share a prefix (`claude` / `claude-work`) stay separate. The new test fails on the merge-base (module missing) and passes on the head. Five of six single-rule reversions of the model are caught by a named assertion. Notifications are sent as an argument vector to `omarchy-notification-send`, not through a shell. The head merges cleanly onto current `quattro`.

The remaining observations concern the QML wiring around the model.

### One reset notification per monitor

`Main` is created inside the bar widget (`shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml:313-316`), and the bar builds one surface per screen. `Bar.qml:468-469` notes that "a widget that appears once in the layout is still live once per screen". Each instance keeps its own `pendingLimitResets` map and 15-second `Timer`:

```text
Bar.qml  Variants { model: Quickshell.screens }
├── BarPanel (screen 1) → agents Panel → Main → pending map + Timer → omarchy-notification-send
└── BarPanel (screen 2) → agents Panel → Main → pending map + Timer → omarchy-notification-send
```

`omarchy.agents` is in the default layout and the setting defaults to on. `omarchy-notification-send` defaults to `replaces_id=0`, and the notification service does no content deduplication.

**Impact:** with N monitors, each reset produces N identical toasts, up to 15 seconds apart. This follows from source; a multi-monitor session was not run.

**Suggested change:** give the pending map and timer a single owner per shell, for example a headless service plugin, or have only one widget instance announce.

### `omarchy bar set ... notifyOnLimitReset false` does not disable it

| Command | Stored value | `setting(...) !== false` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omarchy bar set omarchy.agents notifyOnLimitReset false` | `"false"` (string, `bin/omarchy-bar:357`) | `true` | still enabled |
| `... notifyOnLimitReset false --json` | `false` | `false` | disabled |

Without `--json`, `bin/omarchy-bar` encodes the value with `jq --arg`, and `PluginRegistry.setBarWidget` stores it without coercion. `Main.qml:92` compares with `!== false`.

**Impact:** the plain CLI form, which the plugin README uses for other settings, leaves notifications on.

**Suggested change:** parse the value tolerantly, as this plugin already does for sync (`parseSyncEnabled`) or with `Style.boolToken`. Also add `notifyOnLimitReset` to the settings table in `shell/plugins/agents/README.md`, which does not list it yet.

### Reset toasts bypass Do Not Disturb

`Main.qml` passes no app name, so the helper uses its default `omarchy-action` (`bin/omarchy-notification-send:13`). `NotificationLogic.shouldBypassDnd` returns true for that name regardless of urgency (`shell/plugins/notifications/NotificationLogic.js:34-38`). `Service.qml` documents the bypass as meant for confirmations of an action the user just took.

**Impact:** timer-driven reset toasts, which can arrive at any hour, still pop up during Do Not Disturb.

**Suggested change:** pass a plugin-specific `--app-name` (for example `Agents`) so DND applies.

### Re-enabling does not re-queue deadlines

Turning the setting off stops the timer and clears the queue. Turning it back on only restarts the timer. `scheduleLimitResetNotifications()` runs only on record changes (`recordsChanged()`), which by default happen every 900 seconds or when the panel opens. The same applies to a provider that is disabled across an announce tick and then re-enabled.

**Impact:** a reset that falls between re-enabling and the next record change is not announced. Once that deadline has passed, a later refresh does not queue it.

**Suggested change:** call `scheduleLimitResetNotifications()` when the timer starts and when provider settings change.

### Design questions

- **Which resets to announce:** every window with a future `resetsAt` is announced, whatever its usage. A 3% window produces "Session (5-hour) is available again.", and two Claude windows sharing a deadline produce two toasts (synthetic model inputs). The text implies the limit had been reached. Queuing only windows seen at or near their limit, or merging same-provider resets due in one tick, are possible options.
- **Empty responses that are not transient:** an empty `limits` array always keeps queued deadlines. For Claude, a queued deadline stays in the collector's cache until it passes, so Claude reaches this case only after cache loss. The Codex collector writes `limits: []` without a status for both backend errors and accounts with no windows. After a lasting change (logout, API-key auth, plan change), each already-queued window can still produce one "available again" toast. An explicit "no windows" marker from the collectors would let the model distinguish these cases.

**Optional test improvement:** reverting the `if (!notificationsEnabled) return {}` branch in `schedule()` still passes `test/shell.d/agents-panel-test.sh`. That branch is what runs in QML while notifications are disabled, because the stopped timer never calls `announce()`. The existing "clears stale pending state" assertion covers `announce(..., false)` instead. An assertion that `schedule(..., false)` returns `{}` would cover it.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head against its merge-base, the in-repository collectors, bar and notification plugins, and upstream Quickshell (`execDetached`) and Qt Declarative (timer, JavaScript imports and date parsing) source. The PR's agents panel test ran in an isolated sandbox on the head and the merge-base, together with single-rule mutations and synthetic model scenarios. Node was not available there, so those runs used Deno's Node compatibility layer. The full `./test/all` suite, Quickshell, the notification daemon, multi-monitor behavior and live provider responses were not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
